articles.title: Multi-subregional susceptibility patterns in gliomas using sub-voxel quantitative susceptibility mapping.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate glioma susceptibility patterns and their clinical/pathological correlations using a sub-voxel quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) technique that quantifies the paramagnetic (χpara) and diamagnetic (χdia) components (APART-QSM). MATERIALS AND METHODS: We enrolled 120 pathologically confirmed glioma patients (n = 120; aged 47 ± 13 years, mean ± standard deviation; 51 women) retrospectively and 6 for histologic validation prospectively. χpara/χdia maps were generated. Subregions included peritumoral edema (PE), subdivided into four equidistant subregions, tumor parenchyma (TP), and necrosis, cystic degeneration (CD). Associations between multi-subregional susceptibility and clinicopathological parameters and a conditional inference tree (CIT) model for genotyping were analyzed. RESULTS: Compared to contralateral normal-appearing tissue (CNAT), TP in high-grade and isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)-wild-type gliomas exhibited increased χpara (p ≤ 0.044), low-grade and IDH-mutant gliomas lower χbulk, χpara and χdia (p ≤ 0.015). PE demonstrated lower susceptibility than CNAT (p < 0.001), with χpara/χdia initially decreasing then increasing with peritumoral distance (p ≤ 0.008). Necrosis showed elevated χpara/χdia (p ≤ 0.025), and CD in oligodendrogliomas displayed higher χdia than CNAT (p = 0.019). The CIT model (TP χdia and PE χpara) achieved 0.702 accuracy. Univariable analysis showed that higher TP χpara/χdia correlated with shorter survival (p < 0.001). In the prospective subgroup, TP χpara correlated with iron content (r = 0.901, p = 0.014), TP χdia/χpara correlated with Ki-67 (r = 0.841, p = 0.036). CONCLUSION: APART-QSM revealed distinct, clinically relevant susceptibility profiles across glioma subregions with potential associations with genotyping and prognosis, providing biomarkers for iron content and tumor proliferation. Distance-associated susceptibility pattern in PE may reflect peritumoral microenvironmental properties. KEY POINTS: Question Gliomas exhibit complex histopathology with heterogeneous magnetic susceptibility. Effective preoperative evaluation of multi-subregional susceptibility patterns in gliomas facilitates refined tissue characterization and guides clinical treatment. Findings Glioma subregions showed clinically relevant susceptibility profiles, correlating with iron content, tumor proliferation, and revealing a distance-associated peritumoral edema pattern. Relevance statement Our study used the APART-QSM technique to characterize multi-subregional susceptibility patterns and pathological changes in different glioma types, revealing its potential association with glioma genotyping and prognosis.

articles.title: Characterization of airway mucus using quantitative MRI: an in vitro proof-of-concept study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: A characteristic of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease is mucus hypersecretion. In this proof-of-concept study, we aimed to characterize airway mucus using a quantitative ultrashort echo time (UTE) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) sequence in a controlled in vitro synthetic mucus model to establish a technical foundation for future in vivo studies. MATERIALS AND METHODS: UTE double-echo steady-state (UTE-DESS) was performed to acquire the signal from free induction decay-like signal and spin/stimulated echo-like signal echoes; quantitative MRI parameters (T1, T2, and diffusivity) were estimated. Synthetic mucus phantoms were prepared using mucin (0.20%, 0.50%, and 1.0%) mixed with xanthan gum (0.10%, 0.25%, and 0.50%) to replicate the viscoelastic properties of human laryngeal mucus, and samples were embedded in 1% agar for imaging. RESULTS: The mucus phantoms with varying concentrations of mucin and xanthan exhibited visual differences in color and opacity. Estimated T1 values were 2.23 ± 0.16, 2.37 ± 0.20, and 2.09 ± 0.18 s (mean ± standard deviation) for the three tubes with relative mucus concentrations of 1, 2.5, and 5, respectively. Corresponding T2 values were 806.6 ± 105.6, 687.4 ± 78.0, and 475.0 ± 41.3 ms, while diffusivity values were 2.36 ± 0.14, 2.31 ± 0.18, and 2.33 ± 0.18 µm2/ms for the three tubes. Only the T2 relaxation times showed a significant linear correlation with mucus concentration (r = -0.9998, p = 0.0112). CONCLUSION: UTE-DESS MRI could be feasible for characterizing airway mucus. T2 relaxation time showed a strong inverse correlation with increasing mucus concentration, indicating its sensitivity to mucus content. KEY POINTS: Question Can a novel quantitative ultrashort echo time MRI sequence noninvasively characterize airway mucus properties and overcome conventional lung imaging limitations in muco-obstructive diseases? Findings In this controlled in vitro model, UTE-DESS MRI mapping demonstrated that T2 relaxation times alone showed a strong inverse correlation with increasing mucus concentrations. Relevance statement This exploratory proof-of-concept establishes a technical foundation for radiation-free, noninvasive T2 mapping to monitor and phenotype chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and other mucoobstructive lung diseases in future in vivo studies.

articles.title: Performance of ChatGPT-5 under a minimal binary prompt for detection of distal radius fractures on plain radiographs.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: General-purpose multimodal large language models (LLMs) are being applied to radiology, but their performance under the simplest realistic clinical query (a single binary fracture-or-not prompt) has not been rigorously quantified. We evaluated ChatGPT-5 on this task using a public distal radius dataset. METHODS: In this retrospective diagnostic accuracy study, 396 anteroposterior distal radius radiographs from the Stanford MURA dataset were submitted to ChatGPT-5, each in a fresh temporary chat session. The prompt was: "Is there a fracture in this X-ray? Answer with yes or no." The reference standard was an image-level label assigned by consensus between a senior orthopedic resident and a board-certified orthopedic surgeon; MURA study-level labels were used only to select candidate images. Twenty-six radiographs (6.6%) returned a hedged response and were excluded from the primary analysis, leaving 370; all 26 were added back in three sensitivity analyses. Outcomes were sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, F1, balanced accuracy, and Cohen's kappa, with 95% Wilson confidence intervals and McNemar's test for error asymmetry. RESULTS: Fracture prevalence in the analyzed sample was 45.9% (170/370). Sensitivity was 51.2% (95% CI 43.7-58.6), specificity 70.5% (63.8-76.4), accuracy 61.6% (56.6-66.4), PPV 59.6% (51.5-67.2), NPV 62.9% (56.5-69.0), F1 0.551, Cohen's kappa 0.219 (0.112-0.318). False negatives exceeded false positives (McNemar χ2 = 4.06, p = 0.044). Non-binary responses occurred in 7.6% of fracture-positive and 5.7% of fracture-negative radiographs (p = 0.54); counting all as errors lowered sensitivity to 47.3% (40.2-54.5), and no assumption raised it above 54.9%. Projected to 20% prevalence, PPV was 30.3% and NPV 85.2%. CONCLUSION: Under a minimal binary prompt and without task-specific fine-tuning, ChatGPT-5 missed approximately half of distal radius fractures and fell well below published performance for dedicated CNN-based fracture detectors. Results are specific to this model version, this prompt, this anatomical region, and this dataset; they constrain claims about autonomous, minimal-prompt use rather than the broader potential of engineered LLM-based radiological workflows.

Comparison of Hockey-Stick and Conventional Linear Ultrasound Transducers for Detection of Non-Displaced Dentoalveolar Fractures: An Ex Vivo Paired Comparative Study.
articles.abstract: Objectives: To compare fracture detection rates and observer confidence between a high-frequency hockey-stick transducer and a conventional linear transducer for detecting non-displaced dentoalveolar fractures in a paired ex vivo model. Materials and Methods: This paired ex vivo study included 88 experimentally created non-displaced dentoalveolar fracture sites in fresh ovine specimens. Two oral and maxillofacial radiologists independently evaluated all sites with both a 12L3 conventional linear transducer (10-15 MHz) and an 18H5 hockey-stick transducer (10-18 MHz), with transducer order randomized. Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) confirmed fracture status. Within-observer paired fracture-detection outcomes were compared using the exact McNemar test, and a cluster-adjusted generalized estimating equation (GEE) analysis accounted for repeated assessments and clustering within ovine heads. Observer confidence was compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Results: Observer 1 detected 76/88 fracture sites (86.4%) with the hockey-stick transducer and 64/88 (72.7%) with the conventional linear transducer (p = 0.004). Observer 2 detected 74/88 sites (84.1%) and 62/88 (70.5%), respectively (p < 0.001). In the cluster-adjusted GEE analysis, the hockey-stick transducer was associated with higher odds of fracture detection (OR, 2.29; 95% CI, 1.84-2.86; p < 0.001). For both observers, confidence scores were higher with the hockey-stick transducer (median [IQR], 4 [3-4] vs. 3 [2-3]; both p < 0.001), with Cohen's dz values of 0.849 and 0.791, respectively. In a separate pre-study calibration set, interobserver agreement was 95% (κ = 0.828; 95% CI, 0.503-1.000). Conclusions: In this ex vivo model, the hockey-stick transducer achieved consistently higher fracture-detection rates across both observers and greater observer confidence than the conventional linear transducer. The observed differences may reflect the combined technical and ergonomic characteristics of the two transducers rather than probe geometry alone. Prospective clinical studies including both fractured and non-fractured sites are required before conclusions regarding diagnostic accuracy or clinical superiority can be established.

articles.title: Relative CT Number as a Quantitative Imaging Biomarker for Differentiating Sinonasal Polyp, Inverted Papilloma, and Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Preliminary Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Unilateral sinonasal lesions may be difficult to characterize on non-contrast computed tomography (CT) because inflammatory polyps, benign neoplasms, and malignant tumors can appear as similar unilateral soft-tissue masses. Non-contrast CT is widely available, but the diagnostic performance of relative CT number across inflammatory, benign neoplastic, and malignant sinonasal lesions within a single cohort remains insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to provide additional evidence regarding the diagnostic performance of relative CT number on non-contrast CT by comparing its values among sinonasal polyp (SP), inverted papilloma (IP), and squamous cell carcinoma (SCC), and by evaluating predefined binary diagnostic comparisons. Methods: This retrospective single-center study included 92 patients with histopathologically confirmed unilateral or unilateral-dominant sinonasal lesions: 49 SP, 24 IP, and 19 SCC. Preoperative non-contrast paranasal sinus CT images were reviewed. Relative CT number was calculated as the ratio of mean lesion attenuation to mean pontine attenuation. Group differences were analyzed using non-parametric tests, and diagnostic performance was assessed with receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Age-adjusted binary logistic regression analyses were also performed for the predefined binary comparisons. Sensitivity analyses were additionally adjusted for lesion ROI area. Results: Relative CT number differed significantly among the three groups (overall p < 0.001). ROC analysis showed an AUC of 0.815 (95% CI, 0.704-0.904) for SP versus IP, 0.667 (95% CI, 0.498-0.826) for IP versus SCC, 0.869 (95% CI, 0.792-0.932) for SP versus IP+SCC, and 0.937 (95% CI, 0.866-0.986) for SP versus SCC. After age adjustment, relative CT number was associated with the positive diagnostic category in all four comparisons; however, the IP-SCC association was no longer significant after ROI-area adjustment (p = 0.073). The highest diagnostic performance was observed for distinguishing SP from SCC. Conclusions: These preliminary findings suggest that relative CT number may serve as an adjunctive quantitative CT parameter for differentiating unilateral inflammatory sinonasal lesions from neoplastic lesions, with the strongest diagnostic performance observed for SP versus SCC. However, its standalone discrimination between IP and SCC was limited, and the age-adjusted association remains hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Effect of Simulated Soft-Tissue Edema on Ultrasonographic Detection of Nondisplaced Dentoalveolar Fractures: An Ex Vivo Animal Model Study.
articles.abstract: Objectives: This single-blinded ex vivo diagnostic accuracy study evaluated high-frequency ultrasonography for detecting nondisplaced dentoalveolar fractures and assessed the effect of simulated post-traumatic soft-tissue edema. Methods: Eighteen fresh sheep heads provided 108 anatomically distinct sites (54 fractured and 54 non-fractured controls). Two blinded oral and maxillofacial radiologists independently assessed each site, yielding 216 observer-level evaluations. Cone-beam tomography (CBCT) served as the reference standard. Edema was simulated by submucosal injection of 0.5, 1.0, or 1.5 mL sterile saline. Results: Simulated edema was associated with significantly lower odds of correct ultrasonographic classification in the GEE analysis accounting for within-site clustering (OR = 0.217; 95% CI, 0.096-0.491; p < 0.001). Accuracy decreased from 87.0% to 59.3%, sensitivity from 96.3% to 77.8%, and specificity from 77.8% to 40.7%. False-negative and false-positive rates increased from 3.7% to 22.2% and from 22.2% to 59.3%, respectively. Observer confidence also decreased significantly (3.53 ± 0.90 vs. 2.61 ± 0.86; p < 0.001). No statistically significant differences in diagnostic accuracy were detected among the three edema-volume groups. Conclusions: Simulated soft-tissue edema substantially impairs ultrasonographic detection of nondisplaced dentoalveolar fractures. These experimental findings suggest that negative ultrasonographic findings obtained in the presence of soft-tissue swelling should be interpreted cautiously, with complementary imaging considered when clinically indicated.

articles.title: Preprocedural CT Radiomic Features of the Basal Ganglia Are Associated with Post-Thrombectomy Hyperdense Transformation: A LASSO-Based Logistic Regression Analysis.
articles.abstract: Purpose: To investigate whether radiomic characteristics of visually unremarkable basal ganglia on preprocedural non-contrast computed tomography (CT) are associated with subsequent post-thrombectomy hyperdense transformation (HT) in patients with acute ischemic stroke. Materials and Methods: This retrospective single-center study included a derivation cohort of 84 patients with preserved Alberta Stroke Programme Early CT Scores (ASPECTS ≥ 8), no visually appreciable basal ganglia abnormality, anterior circulation large-vessel occlusion, and complete reperfusion after mechanical thrombectomy between January 2022 and July 2023. An independent temporal validation cohort comprised 31 consecutive eligible patients treated between August and November 2023. The ipsilateral basal ganglia were manually segmented on preprocedural non-contrast CT, and radiomic features were extracted using LIFEx. Candidate features underwent interobserver reproducibility assessment and correlation filtering before least absolute shrinkage and selection operator logistic regression with 10-fold cross-validation. The final model was applied without modification to the temporal validation cohort. Nested cross-validation and learning-curve analysis were additionally performed to assess model-development optimism and stability. Results: The final model retained two texture features, Gray-Level Run Length Matrix Short Runs Emphasis and Gray-Level Size Zone Matrix Grey Level Variance. In the derivation cohort, the model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.760 (95% CI, 0.652-0.855), with 48.8% sensitivity, 95.3% specificity, and 72.6% accuracy. When applied without modification to the independent temporal validation cohort, the AUC was 0.677 (95% CI, 0.475-0.858), with 33.3% sensitivity, 93.8% specificity, and 64.5% accuracy. Nested cross-validation yielded a mean AUC of 0.673 ± 0.037, with variability in feature selection across resampling iterations. Learning-curve analysis showed an early plateau, with little improvement in cross-validated discrimination as the training sample increased within the evaluated range. Conclusions: Radiomic analysis of visually unremarkable basal ganglia on preprocedural non-contrast CT identified an exploratory two-feature imaging signature associated with subsequent post-thrombectomy HT. The model retained modest discriminatory ability in temporal validation, although internal resampling demonstrated model-development optimism and limited feature-selection stability. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and warrant further evaluation using larger datasets, alternative modeling approaches, and independent multicenter validation.

articles.title: CT Radiomics and Machine Learning for Three-Class Bone Density Classification: An Exploratory Comparison Across Lumbar Vertebral Levels.
articles.abstract: Objectives: The aim of this study is to provide early diagnosis of osteoporosis, osteopenia, and normal bone mineral density (BMD) on CT scans utilizing machine learning and radiomics techniques. Methods: In this retrospective study, 874 patients who met the predefined eligibility criteria were included. BMD was categorized as normal, osteopenia, or osteoporosis according to DEXA-derived T-scores. Lumbar vertebral bodies were automatically segmented on abdominal and lumbar CT images, and radiomic features were extracted from the segmented regions. Logistic regression (LR), decision table (DT), random forest (RF), multilayer perceptron (MLP), and bagging models were developed to distinguish among the three BMD categories. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, F-score, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC area), and area under the precision-recall curve (PRC area). Results: Notably, the best results were observed in the L3 vertebra among the 874 patients included in the study. Accordingly, the MLP and LR methods showed the greatest accuracy value of 83.5%, F-score value of 81.2%, ROC area value of 0.912, and PRC area value of 0.892 in cases with normal BMD. At the L2 vertebral level, the LR approach produced the greatest results for patients with osteoporosis (Acc: 72.5%, F-score: 72.5%, ROC area: 0.897, and PRC area: 0.797). Conclusions: In the three-class BMD assessment, the models showed the highest performance for normal BMD and the lowest performance for osteopenia. Among the individual lumbar levels, L3 demonstrated the highest radiomics-based classification performance, whereas L1 showed comparatively lower performance. These level-specific findings should be regarded as exploratory and should not be interpreted as supporting clinical BMD classification from a single vertebra. CT radiomics may have potential as an opportunistic screening tool to identify patients who may benefit from formal DEXA or further osteoporosis evaluation; however, patient-level multivertebral validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted ACR TI-RADS Assessment of Thyroid Nodules: Potential for Reducing Unnecessary Biopsies in a Prospective Single-Center Study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based ultrasound risk stratification has emerged as a promising tool for improving the evaluation of thyroid nodules. However, prospective evidence regarding its performance in routine clinical practice and its potential impact on biopsy recommendations remains limited. METHODS: In this prospective single-center observational study, 1009 thyroid nodules undergoing ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration between May 2025 and May 2026 were independently evaluated using ChatGPT Plus as an investigational AI-assisted decision-support tool. Representative ultrasound images, including dimensional and Doppler images, were submitted to the AI without disclosure of the radiologist-assigned TI-RADS category or subsequent cytological or histopathological findings. AI-assisted and radiologist-assigned TI-RADS classifications were compared with Bethesda cytology, while postoperative histopathology served as the reference standard in the surgically treated subgroup. Diagnostic performance and discordance in risk classification between AI and routine radiologist assessment were evaluated. RESULTS: The study included 1009 thyroid nodules from patients with a mean age of 51.5 ± 13.4 years, of whom 80.7% were female. Bethesda II was the most frequent cytological category (93.6%). AI classified 227 nodules (22.5%) as high risk (TR4-TR5), compared with 761 nodules (75.5%) by routine radiologist assessment (p < 0.001). Among Bethesda II nodules, AI assigned 172 (18.2%) to TR4-TR5 compared with 701 (74.2%) by radiologists. When ACR TI-RADS category-specific size thresholds were applied, FNA would have been recommended for 469 nodules (46.5%) according to AI-assisted classification and 993 nodules (98.4%) according to radiologist-assigned classification (p < 0.001), corresponding to 524 fewer modeled FNA recommendations with AI-assisted assessment. Histopathological evaluation was available for 73 surgically treated nodules, including 48 malignant and 25 benign lesions. Within this surgically verified subgroup, both AI-assisted and radiologist-assigned TI-RADS achieved a sensitivity of 100.0%, while specificity was 72.0% for AI-assisted assessment and 60.0% for radiologist assessment. Because histopathological verification was available only for surgically treated nodules, these diagnostic performance estimates apply specifically to the surgically verified subgroup and cannot exclude false-negative disease among nonoperated nodules. CONCLUSIONS: AI-assisted ACR TI-RADS assessment produced substantially fewer high-risk assignments than routine radiologist assessment, with the greatest divergence observed among cytologically benign nodules. These findings suggest a potential role for AI as a second-reader decision-support tool for refining thyroid nodule risk stratification and biopsy selection. However, because all nodules had already undergone FNA and histopathological verification was limited to surgically treated cases, the present study cannot establish the safety of AI-guided biopsy de-escalation or exclude false-negative disease among nonoperated nodules. Prospective management studies with longitudinal outcome verification are required to determine whether AI-assisted assessment can safely reduce unnecessary FNA.

articles.title: CT-Referenced Diagnostic Performance and Complementary Error Patterns of Artificial Intelligence Versus a Single Emergency Physician in Chest Radiograph Interpretation: A Retrospective Paired Diagnostic Accuracy Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to support chest radiograph interpretation, but its clinical value depends not only on stand-alone accuracy but also on whether its errors differ from those of clinicians. We evaluated CT-referenced, target-specific diagnostic performance and complementary error patterns of a commercial chest radiograph AI system and a single emergency physician. Methods: In this retrospective, single-center, paired diagnostic accuracy study, 920 consecutive adults who underwent posteroanterior chest radiography and thoracic computed tomography (CT) within 4 h during the same emergency department encounter were included. A commercial AI system (hChestXR version 1) and a single blinded emergency physician independently assessed eight prespecified thoracic findings using CT as the reference standard. Paired differences were estimated with 10,000 patient-level bootstrap resamples and tested with exact McNemar tests with Holm adjustment. Exact-target complementarity and simulated same-target OR/AND rules were secondary exploratory analyses. Results: Across 7360 patient-target assessments, including 1232 CT-positive findings, AI had significantly greater Holm-adjusted sensitivity for pneumothorax (90.8% vs. 50.8%), nodule/mass (63.3% vs. 32.7%), and rib fracture (77.2% vs. 46.5%). AI-only detections were most frequent for pneumothorax (47.7%), nodule/mass (44.9%), and rib fracture (43.6%), whereas physician-only detections were most frequent for atelectasis (24.8%), pulmonary edema (21.0%), and lung opacity (19.7%). In exploratory pooled analyses, sensitivity was 73.0% for AI and 62.0% for the physician. Exploratory simulated same-target OR/AND analyses demonstrated a sensitivity-specificity trade-off across pooled patient-target assessments but did not represent observed AI-assisted clinical performance. Conclusions: The AI system and the single emergency-physician reader in the study showed target-dependent, partly non-overlapping error patterns in this CT-selected emergency cohort. The findings support prospective multireader evaluation of AI as a second-reader tool but do not establish benefit from real-time AI-assisted interpretation.

articles.title: Evaluation of Parameters Relevant to Paraclinoid Microsurgery: Morphometric Analysis of the Anterior, Middle, and Posterior Clinoid Processes.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The paraclinoid region-bounded by the anterior clinoid process (ACP), middle clinoid process (MCP), posterior clinoid process (PCP), optic strut (OS), and sella turcica-is critical in skull base anatomy owing to its proximity to the optic nerve, internal carotid artery (ICA), and cavernous sinus. Because the bony anatomy of this region varies considerably between individuals, detailed morphometric characterization is a prerequisite for anticipating the working corridor before anterior clinoidectomy and related approaches. This study aimed (1) to quantify the morphometric parameters of the optic canal (CO) and the ACP, MCP, and PCP using computed tomography angiography (CTA), (2) to test right-left and sex-based differences and topographic correlations among these parameters and cranial dimensions, and (3) to derive exploratory morphometric classifications of ACP shape and the ACP-OS relationship. Methods: High-resolution CTA images from 102 patients (204 sides) were retrospectively analyzed. Bilateral morphometric measurements were obtained for the CO and the ACP, MCP, and PCP, together with bilateral and ipsilateral interclinoid distances and cranial (biparietal, fronto-occipital) diameters. Data were analyzed with descriptive statistics, right-left and sex-stratified comparisons, and Pearson correlations. ACP pneumatization was classified into four types, and three exploratory, data-derived classifications-the Anteroclinoid Morphometric Index (AMI), ACP Size Score (ASS), and Paraclinoid Access Index (PAI)-were constructed from the linear measurements. Results: ACP basal width, length, ACP-OS distance, and CO-level basal width were symmetric and sex-independent, whereas the ACP-PCP and ACP-MCP distances were significantly greater on the left (p = 0.015 and p < 0.001), a pattern more pronounced in men. ACP pneumatization was most commonly absent (Type 0; 79.4% right, 82.4% left) and did not differ by side or sex. Bilateral interclinoid distances correlated with one another and, more strongly in men, with biparietal diameter. The ASS and, more weakly, the PAI correlated with the ipsilateral ACP-MCP distance (right ASS-ACP-MCP r = 0.382, p < 0.001; left r = 0.312, p = 0.001) and with CO transverse diameter, chiefly on the left (ASS r = 0.232, p = 0.019; PAI r = 0.352, p < 0.001), indicating that these indices track broader topographic variation in the paraclinoid complex rather than the ACP alone. The predominant bilateral categories were AMI-2 (39.2%), ASS-2 (31.4%), and PAI-2 (61.8%). Conclusions: ACP, MCP, and PCP morphometry in this cohort was largely symmetric, with a consistent left-sided predominance restricted to the ACP-PCP and ACP-MCP distances. The AMI, ASS, and PAI are exploratory, data-derived classifications-not validated surgical indices-that provide a quantitative framework for describing ACP morphology and its relationship to the optic strut; whether they carry independent value for predicting surgical corridor width or complication risk has not been tested against operative outcomes and requires prospective validation.

articles.title: Deep Learning-Based Reconstruction in Ultra-Low-Dose CT of the Ankle and Foot: A Comparative Study with Hybrid Iterative Reconstruction.
articles.abstract: Objectives: To evaluate the quantitative and qualitative performance of ultra-low-dose CT with deep learning image reconstruction (DLR) compared to conventional hybrid iterative reconstruction (IR) in patients with ankle and foot fractures. Methods: A total of 32 patients (mean age, 54 ± 16 years) with ankle and foot fractures were included in this retrospective study. All patients underwent ultra-low-dose CT imaging (effective dose, 0.86 ± 0.11 μSv), and the same CT raw data were reconstructed using both DLR and hybrid IR. Image noise, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) were quantitatively measured, and image sharpness was evaluated using a no-reference perceptual sharpness metric. Subjective image quality was assessed by a board-certified radiologist and an orthopedic surgeon using a five-point scale. Results: DLR significantly reduced image noise (47.33 ± 6.60 HU) compared to hybrid IR (87.65 ± 12.48 HU), and significantly improved SNR (31.42 ± 5.81 for DLR vs. 19.15 ± 4.48 for hybrid IR) and CNR (50.59 ± 7.62 for DLR vs. 24.08 ± 3.81 for hybrid IR). Image sharpness was significantly (p = 0.001) improved with DLR (0.76 ± 0.09) compared to hybrid IR (0.59 ± 0.09). Subjective image analysis revealed enhanced visualization of trabecular architecture, superior delineation and integrity of cortical bone, and improved depiction of bony cortical lesions with DLR compared to hybrid IR. Conclusions: Ultra-low-dose CT with DLR offers a superior approach to enhance image quality, making it a valuable tool for clinical practice.

Black-Blood Cinematic Rendering of the Pulmonary Vasculature: A Negative-Contrast Intraluminal Preset.
articles.abstract: Cinematic rendering (CR) is a physically based three-dimensional (3D) computed tomography (CT) visualization technique that has been applied chiefly to the external surface morphology of vascular structures. Intraluminal CR has previously been described for the cardiac chambers as black-blood cinematic rendering (BBCR), in which the opacity assigned to the contrast-enhanced blood pool is suppressed. Here, we describe the adaptation of that principle to the pulmonary vasculature as a negative-contrast intraluminal preset, in which the opacified blood pool is rendered semi-transparent so that the vessel lumen is displayed as a low-signal channel delineated by the enhancing vessel wall. We report the acquisition and rendering conditions under which the appearance was obtained in a single illustrative case performed for chest pain and showing no pulmonary vascular pathology, together with the rendering platform, base preset, and lighting configuration; the attenuation-band settings that define the appearance were tuned for the individual examination rather than applied as a fixed parameter set, were not recorded, and cannot be supplied as numerical values, so a stepwise construction procedure is given in their place. Intermediate rather than maximal compartment-specific opacification was required for the transfer function to separate lumen from wall; the case presented was acquired in an early pulmonary arterial phase, and a late split-bolus acquisition is an alternative route to the same condition that was not used here. In the case presented, the lumen of segmental and up to third-order subsegmental pulmonary arterial and venous branches was visually demonstrated on qualitative assessment by a single reader, and the preset remained stable when applied unchanged across the reconstructed 40-80% R-R window for four-dimensional display, which is a partial rather than a complete cardiac cycle reconstruction. Preset construction was less successful at the central pulmonary arteries and veins, where dense opacification and proximity to the cardiac blood pool reduced the contrast available to the transfer function. This is a single-case technical description. It demonstrates that the appearance can be produced under defined conditions and sets out the procedure by which it was constructed; it does not establish that the exact parameter values are recoverable or transferable, and it does not establish diagnostic performance, which will require prospective comparison against conventional reformats in adequately powered studies.
